source.title: Structurally Close, Security-Wise Far: Contradictory Policies in Neural Networks

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops theoretical results about structural edits in constructed neural networks. It cites refusal-direction work and studies related directional-ablation ideas, but it does not test refusal in chat models or the claim versions as stated.
record.gate_note: The paper's own direction-ablation results concern constructed gated networks and abstract safe/unsafe target policies, not refusal rates on harmful or harmless instructions. References to earlier refusal-direction results are cited background, not results of this study.
record.test_reason: Purely theoretical paper (no experiments, no datasets, no code) on structural security distance between masks in constructed networks. Its direction results concern a hand-built gated linear layer with abstract safe/unsafe target policies, not a difference-in-means refusal direction in a language model. It cites Arditi et al. 2024 only as background and says directional ablation itself is established. None of its own results measure refusal rates or bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors also conclude that a globally close safe/unsafe mask pair does not imply that a deployed mask is close to an unsafe one, and that estimating normalized structural security distance is NP-hard in the worst case. They add that one-toggle bounds can certify safety within a stated number of edits, and that audits should state which masks and edits are allowed and whether distances are certified or estimated.
record.recipe_differences: The paper provides theoretical constructions and bounds for mask-based structural distance, rather than applying the original difference-in-means refusal-direction method to chat models.
record.method_sensitivity: Theoretical bounds depend on direction coordinate concentration, approximation tolerance, security-domain alignment, and (for benign-path barriers) assumptions on benign representations.

fits_no_version.finding: In a constructed gated linear layer, a one-dimensional direction whose ablation switches policy while preserving benign outputs can require Θ(d) binary neuron-gate edits. One-gate-at-a-time paths can incur a constant benign-error barrier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-dimensional activation-space localization of a safety behavior does not imply that few neuron-level edits suffice to switch it; the cost depends on the direction's coordinate concentration.

record.problems: The results are theoretical constructions and worst-case bounds, not empirical evaluations of trained chat models. The paper explicitly says it uses no experimental datasets or code; the direction-ablation discussion does not measure refusal or general capability in language models.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant own results identified beyond the theoretical direction/gate results recorded above. Cited prior-work findings were not recorded as this study's results.

untested.parts: No diff-in-means direction, no LLM, no refusal rates, no addition, no capability evaluation.
No weight-edit ablation on released models.
No multi-direction comparison; it only remarks that extending the bounds to k-dimensional subspaces would need coordinate concentration.
Not examined; the limitations section excludes training dynamics.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/discusses is right. All rows are theoretical results, kept only as context; none should be linked to a version. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction or refusal behavior in safety-trained chat models is tested; no direction addition is tested.
No weight-edit ablation or released-model refusal evaluation.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation is evaluated.
No comparison of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
No harmfulness judgment or refusal-decision representation is examined.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No refusal training dynamics or training-stage comparison.

rows.subject: Fm(x) = g(x) + (m ⊙ v)⊤ h(x) gate family
rows.operation_detail: Lower-bounds the Hamming distance between feasible safe and unsafe gate masks.

conditions.value: unit v; sup on R of ||h(x)-v||2 ≤ ρ

rows.measure: Minimum safe/unsafe neuron-gate edits; stated example gives a lower bound of 766 edits.
rows.value: At least ceil((d/μ(v)) max{1−2Qε,ρ, 0}) edits; example lower bound: 766.
rows.note: A theoretical structural-distance result for an abstract gate family, not a refusal measurement.
rows.check: Theoretical lower bound on gate edits in an abstract gate family. It is not a measurement of refusal, and 'observed' is not meaningful for any version. Baseline is not applicable.

rows.subject: fixed d-neuron gated linear representation, Fm0,m
rows.size_stated: d neuron gates plus one additional mask coordinate m0
rows.operation_detail: Applies the orthogonal projection I−vv⊤ to ablate the one-dimensional direction v.
rows.value: Projection maps the safe readout to the unsafe target fu(u,z)=(u,0) and preserves every benign output.
rows.note: This is a constructed network with abstract opposite policies, not a chat model or refusal-rate test.
rows.check: Proof, by construction, that projection switches between abstract target policies in a toy gated network. It is not an empirical refusal-direction result and should not be read as V1 evidence.

rows.subject: fixed d-neuron gated linear representation, Fm0,m
rows.size_stated: d neuron gates plus one additional mask coordinate m0
rows.operation_detail: Computes feasible safe/unsafe mask distances and the benign-error barrier along one-gate edit paths.
rows.measure: Minimum mask distance, fixed-safe-mask distance, and maximum benign error on a discrete edit path.
rows.value: Dε,εsec=d−2rε; Dεfixed=d−rε; path benign-error lower bound is sqrt(floor(d²/4))/d. At zero tolerance, Dsec=d/(d+2)→1.
rows.note: The result concerns binary structural edits in the constructed gated model; continuous directional ablation has zero benign error.
rows.check: Derived mask-distance formulas for the constructed network, not a refusal measurement.

rows.subject: Fm(x) = g(x) + (m ⊙ v)⊤ h(x) gate family
rows.operation_detail: Derives a structural-distance lower bound and a benign-error barrier for one-gate-at-a-time paths.
rows.measure: Gate edits between feasible policies; benign error along continuous and discrete paths.
rows.value: At least 954 gate changes; continuous directional path benign error at most 0.04; every one-neuron-edit path has benign error at least 0.38; mask security margin at least 0.35.
rows.note: These are theoretical guarantees and an illustration for the specified gated-layer assumptions, not empirical chat-model results.
rows.check: Numbers come from a numerical illustration of a theorem under assumed parameters, not from data on any model.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
